articles.title: Switch 2 Won’t Get Another Price Hike, At Least Not Soon, Nintendo Says
articles.summary: As part of Nintendo's latest earnings briefing, the company said it has no plans to increase the Switch 2 price again, or at least not anytime soon. VGC reported that management said Nintendo has enough memory stockpiled to shield itself and thus not need to implement another price hike.
body: Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 in September, bringing it up from $450 to $500. This followed price hikes for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles, meaning that all three major platforms have seen hikes.

The price increases are the result of macroeconomic factors including tariffs and the demand for memory and components from AI companies. Following the US midterm elections, technology stocks--and specifically AI stocks--have massively sold off, at least temporarily. It remains to be seen when or if there would be any relief on the memory and component market, though.

Nintendo also reported in its earnings briefing that it received many millions in tariff refunds, but the company is keeping all of it for themselves, just like PlayStation and other companies are doing with their own refunds. Nintendo had a tone-deaf and cringey tariff sale.
Nintendo's latest big game release was The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake for Switch 2, and it's the best-reviewed game of 2026 overall.
points: As part of Nintendo's latest earnings briefing, the company said it has no plans to increase the Switch 2 price again, or at least not anytime soon.
VGC reported that management said Nintendo has enough memory stockpiled to shield itself and thus not need to implement another price hike.

articles.title: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life Drops to a New Low
articles.summary: One of the best wireless gaming headsets just dropped to its lowest price ever. Woot, which is owned by Amazon, is offering a new Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for PS5, PS4, and PC for just $183.99 after you apply 20% off coupon code " PCGAMING ".
body: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro has long been one of IGN's highest rated wireless gaming headsets. IGN's Kevin Lee gave the Nova Pro a 10/10 "Masterpiece" review and I believe it still holds today. I've clocked well over a thousand hours on mine to the point that my earcups were worn through (I replaced them with the awesome WC Freeze gel earpads ). SteelSeries released a successor - the Nova Pro Omni - earlier this year, but it currently sells for $380 and the improvements are certainly not worth the nearly $200 price premium. The Omni's pièce de résistance is its seamless cross-platform switching. If you predominantly use these headphones for one platform, then stick with the Nova Pros.

The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system. The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. This way, you get wireless freedom with zero downtime. Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.
points: One of the best wireless gaming headsets just dropped to its lowest price ever.

articles.title: Pokémon Cards Get Official Induction Into National Toy Hall of Fame
articles.summary: The National Toy Hall of Fame has officially announced this year’s inductees, and one of the biggest trading card games of all time has finally made the cut. Pokémon cards were inducted into the Toy Hall of Fame on the morning of Thursday, November 5, as the franchise celebrates its 30th…
body: "Pokémon TCG’s widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," said curator Mirek Stolee. "The Pokémon TCG successfully adapted card game formulas established by its predecessors, making it more accessible and infusing it with the lovable Pokémon creatures."

The National Toy Hall of Fame was established in 1998 to "recognize toys that have inspired creative play and enjoyed popularity over a sustained period." The Hall of Fame is currently housed at the Strong Museum of Play in Rochester, New York, which is also home to the World Video Game Hall of Fame.

Anyone can nominate a toy for consideration. A panel of museum curators, historians, and educators then evaluate these nominees based on four pillars: icon status, longevity, discovery, and innovation. The Hall of Fame has a relatively loose definition of a toy, having previously inducted a cardboard box and the concept of 'sand' in addition to classics like LEGO, Barbies, and slinkies.

This isn’t the first time a trading card game has made it onto the prestigious toy list. Magic: The Gathering was added in 2019, nearly 10 years after the induction of another tabletop classic, Dungeons & Dragons.

articles.title: GTA 6 Looks Pretty Realistic, Until It Comes To Gym Etiquette
articles.summary: Compared to previous games in the series, Grand Theft Auto 6 looks like it'll only be a few steps removed from reality when it launches this month. Actions have consequences, working on a relationship requires more than just hitting a few button prompts, and bulking up means that you'll have to…
body: While I keep telling myself that comparison is the thief of joy and that I shouldn't compare the few strands of muscle fiber I have next to a digital character who looks like he curls Jack Reacher actors for a morning routine, I also can't help but find myself repulsed by Jason's lack of hygiene.

I'm also told that Miami--the city that GTA 6's location of Vice City is inspired by--is hot as hell, but that's still no excuse to not be wearing any gym clothing up top. Hell, even if it's one of those gym tank tops with spaghetti straps, that's still better than nothing, because I cannot imagine how much disinfectant you'd need to clean up that rack when Jason is done with it.

There's no sign of a sweat towel either, so you just know there's going to be a rank puddle of perspiration waiting for the next unlucky person who uses it. Revolting. Maybe it's his home gym, but that's still no excuse to work out in this state. Sure, maybe he's the only person who uses that facility, but I bet you the nearby NPCs are going to smell it from across the block.

articles.title: Rapper Kodak Black Will Be in NPC in GTA 6, Creating Speculation Over Other Artists Appearing In-Game
articles.summary: Rapper Kodak Black has been confirmed to be featured as an NPC in GTA 6 via a new batch of screenshots. Rockstar Games released a batch of 39 new screenshots from GTA 6 to celebrate the game being two weeks away from launch, and one of them reveals that Kodak Black will be in the game.
body: It has been heavily speculated that this club would feature a variety of real-world artists, and the confirmation of Kodak Black seems to only add fuel to that speculation. It doesn't seem like a leap to imagine that other artists like Scott or other rappers featured on the game's soundtrack could also appear in-game. There's some precedent for this in previous GTA titles, too.

In GTA Online, Dr Dre appeared as a character that the player could do missions for. The game's nightclubs also featured real DJs such as Solomun, Tale of Us, and Dixon, so it's entirely possible Rockstar managed to get these artists to do real performances at clubs in the game. We'll ultimately have to wait and see, but it's clear that Rockstar has spared no expense with the talent for this game. While there will be some fresh faces in the cast, actor Stephen Root confirmed earlier this year that he will play Brian Heder in GTA 6. The character is expected to be Jason's boss and a drug runner.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever's Launch Was Running on Over 200,000 Gigabytes of RAM
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever launched last night, and while there were a ton of people playing, the servers were remarkably stable. It turns out that Blizzard dedicated a ton of resources to making sure those servers were solid.
body: Last night, after the game launched, Blizzard tweeted out a meme from its World of Warcraft account, with a Gnome tapping a car with the WoW Forever logo, with a caption saying: "*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever* This baby is running on: 3,924 Virtual Machines, 251,136 GB of Memory, 70,480 CPU Cores." That's a huge amount of memory, and it seems to have paid off with the smoothest Blizzard launch I've seen in years.

Blizzard's post bragging about the sheer amount of memory in its servers comes just a week after Sam Altman said in a podcast that it was "quite terrible" for people to have RAM in their own computers, rather than in a data center. Of course, he did later walk it back, instead claiming that he had "been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time." Still, that's 251,136GB of RAM that's dedicated to running an incredible MMO, rather than powering yet another data center.

articles.title: Arkane Union Accuses Microsoft Of “Sabotaging” Development Of Marvel’s Blade
articles.summary: As the fate of Arkane Lyon hangs in the balance, a union representing workers from the French studio offered strong words toward Arkane's parent company, Microsoft. In short, the union blames Microsoft for "sabotaging" the production of its Blade game.
body: French trade union STJV (per VGC ) claimed that development on Marvel's Blade is "going fine," but said that workers face the "harsh reality" that Microsoft may close the studio for financial reasons. But the union said that the onus for Arkane's tough financial situation is on Microsoft itself, claiming that a hiring freeze that lasted 19 months "artificially caused delay and additional cost."

STJV asserts that closing Arkane would be more costly than finishing Marvel's Blade, adding that a studio closure would be the result of Microsoft's "never-ending search for maximum profit optimization." The union argues that Arkane is profitable, but "not profitable enough for Microsoft."

The union's statement lists demands that include protections for employees and giving workers a say in a potential buyer for Arkane. In accordance with French labor laws, the studio has been in a "consultation period" since Xbox began its reset earlier this year, and it was recently granted an extra month to find a buyer before facing closure. A recent report suggests that three companies, including Ubisoft, submitted bids to acquire Arkane.
points: As the fate of Arkane Lyon hangs in the balance, a union representing workers from the French studio offered strong words toward Arkane's parent company, Microsoft.

articles.title: Major Pokémon Center TCG Orders Delayed At The Last Minute
articles.summary: Pokémon Trading Card Game fans have spent the last couple of days feeling anxious. Delta Reign, the next big TCG set, releases on Friday — and The Pokémon Center hasn't updated anyone about their orders.
body: There are three major Delta Reign products set to release on Friday, Nov. 6: the Elite Trainer Box, Booster Bundles, and Booster Boxes. Pokémon Center ETBs, which come with extra packs and promo cards, are particularly prized by fans and resellers.

Pokémon customers from the U.K. recently received a notice from TPC informing them about delays for all three items. The company now says that its Delta Reign products will ship sometime in mid-November, but has not share any specifics beyond that.

Customers in the United States, however, have not been informed of issues with orders yet. Given the lack of charges and shipping updates, it seems likely that it is only a matter of time before TPC breaks the news to everyone. As of this writing, TPC's website is undergoing extensive maintenance.

According to Pokémon fans sharing their communications with TPC customer support, the delays are due to an internal mix-up. The storefront apparently told a number of customers that they had to reauthorize payments despite, in some cases, not actually needing additional information. This may also explain why the TPC website's checkout function hasn't worked for nearly a week.

articles.title: D&D’s World of Warcraft Designer Hid a Personal Easter Egg in Plain Sight
articles.summary: Mounts in World of Warcraft are status symbols, a way of showing off the challenging raids you’ve completed or how far in the PvP ranks you’ve climbed. Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft lead designer James Wyatt couldn’t help showing off himself a bit in the book’s art, where he slipped in an…
body: Fortunately, getting those rare cosmetic items is much easier in the Dungeons & Dragons expansion than in WoW. A character proficient in history can spend an hour or a short rest searching the site of Highmountain Tauren ruins for Archaeology fragments. If they gather six, they can be assembled into a staff that casts the Find Steed spell, summoning the famed moose once ridden by the Tauren hero Huln Highmountain. Wyatt also lets players acquire the Cenarion War Hippogryph, another mount he spent a lot of effort on, by raising their Renown with the Cenarion Circle through protecting the natural balance of Azeroth.

“Cosmetic rewards in WoW are about bragging rights, which is an individual achievement, and D&D is not a game about individual achievements. It's a game about stuff you do as a group together,” Wyatt told Polygon in a virtual interview. “Having mounts appear as Renown rewards and other special things was important for the feel of this cool element of WoW that I want to see in D&D, but the sort of rare achievement aspect of it falls into the category of mechanics that we didn't try to translate.”

articles.title: Nintendo says it isn't planning any more Switch 2 price hikes
articles.summary: Nintendo, which unveiled the results of the first half of its fiscal year 2027 earlier today, has now said it has access to enough quantities of memory to manufacture more Switch 2 consoles.
body: As a result, the platform holder does not plan to increase the price of the Switch 2. That's according to Reuters, citing Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa.

Nintendo, which has so far sold 26m Switch 2 consoles, has already raised the price of the console earlier this year. The price hikes, which took effect on 1st September in the US, Canada, Japan and Europe, saw the console's price increase by $50 / €30 / ¥10,000. Although that was technically the first price hike for the console itself, prior to the Switch 2's launch last year, Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 accessories in the US as a result of the Trump Administration's tariffs.
The reason that would cause Nintendo to raise prices again is the same that already caused rival PlayStation and Xbox to do so: AI-driven, global memory and storage shortages.

PlayStation already raised PS5 and PS5 Pro prices, on several occasions. Xbox has likewise gone through multiple rounds of price hikes for its Series X and Series S consoles, with the most recent having taken place in August.

articles.title: How to change the time of day in Zelda Ocarina of Time
articles.summary: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, you need to change the time of day to complete certain missions. The people of Hyrule are living their lives while Link is trying to save the world. As a result, the availability of places and characters change depending on the time of the day.
body: Instead of waiting for the in-game time to pass naturally, we can make it happen with a few notes. Here's how to change the time of day in the Ocarina of Time remake.
Although time in Ocarina of Time passes as you play the game, you can actively change from daytime to nighttime by using two methods: sleeping and playing the Sun's Song.

To sleep, you simply need to find beds that you can sleep on, such as the one inside the purple-doored house on the northwestern side of Hyrule Castle Town. Interact with the bed, and a menu will appear with the option to sleep. You will only be able to choose between sleeping until morning or until night after talking to Zelda in Hyrule Castle and completing the "Princess of Hyrule Castle" quest.

Sleeping is always a solid option for changing time, since Link will also recover hearts for free. However, you won't always have a bed nearby, and backtracking to a city just to sleep is not the best idea in most situations. Because of that, you should use the Sun's Song.

articles.title: 'What!?': Ocarina of Time Producer Admits Even the Zelda Team Was Shocked At Art Changes
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ’ s new Switch 2 remake is out now, and it’s already winning players over. It’s the best reviewed game of 2026 by a wide margin, and social media feeds are already filling up with nostalgic posts as players discover a classic game.
body: If you initially weren’t sure what to think about Ocarina of Time ’s new look, the developers behind the project understand. In an interview with Polygon, longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma explained that the Zelda series’ constant art direction shifts can take the team itself off guard. But Aonuma believes that the cycle of shock and acceptance is very much part of the Zelda ethos.

When the Ocarina of Time remake was announced, players were immediately torn over its art — just as they were when Star Fox was revealed earlier this year. Snap reactions characterized the game as a typical Unreal Engine makeover with “Nintendo, hire this man!” energy. In discussing that with Aonuma, I mentioned that the reaction felt similar to that of Wind Waker when it was first revealed decades ago. Initially, the adventure’s cel-shaded art drew criticism from fans upon release who expected a more realistic Zelda game on GameCube. That judgment has aged poorly, considering that Wind Waker ’s look is now widely hailed as timeless, but Aonuma empathizes with that cycle.

Aion 2, another MMO released back in October, is sitting pretty at around 75,900 viewers, while Nintendo's newly released The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake ( it's good! ) has brought in a wonderful 63,100 watchers on the day of its arrival.

Perhaps contributing to World of Warcraft: Forever's success is the fact it launched with few problems, enjoying one of the smoothest day-one releases in the series' recent history. articles.title: EA's releasing a truckload of classic games on Steam, and 7 of them are remasters
articles.summary: Last month we got news that Wing Commander 3, the FMV space-combat sim with perhaps the highest concentration of Mark Hamill in any videogame, would be getting a remaster. Producer Jim Vessella is heading up the project, and revealed it during a presentation at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo.
body: What he did not reveal, it turns out, is that five other Wing Commander games—plus Road Rash—would be getting their own dolled-up re-releases, and that they'd all be dropping on Steam, GOG, and the EA App today as part of a larger bundle of 25 "EA Classics". No, I don't know why you'd buy them on the EA App either. It takes all sorts to make a world.
Here's the full list of games that are dropping. Anything labelled "Anniversary Edition" is an updated, remastered version of the original game. Anything not labelled that is simply a re-release.

If you're a GOG user, the only new things on that storefront will be the remasters—GOG's had all the other classic games for yonks now, but on Steam it's a veritable deluge of hearty, classic stuff. Personally, I'll just be glad to have a copy of Theme Hospital where all my other games are. And if someone fancies turning on Workshop support for it and integrating CorsixTH, they won't hear any objections from me.
